one_liner: Senior press ombudsman for Stars and Stripes who protects its editorial independence, investigates censorship and fairness complaints, and writes public columns on journalism issues.
fit_summary: The posting requires extensive journalism experience and over 10 years as a senior editorial leader, and nothing on file shows Daniel has a journalism background. Daniel's policy knowledge, people skills and familiarity with Congress match some preferred qualifications, but those cannot replace the core requirement.
eligibility: Open to the public (NAF position); outside applicants are considered after NAF priority groups such as Business Based Action and current or former NAF employees.
Must have extensive experience as a journalist plus over 10 years as a senior editorial leader.
Must have one year of experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level.
No security clearance is required, but international travel is required.
keywords: free flow of news and information
strategy: Be honest with yourself first: apply only if you have real journalism or editorial leadership experience that is not on file, because the questionnaire answers are checked against your resume.

If you lack that background, put your effort into better-matched roles such as FEMA or Virginia VDEM program and outreach jobs, constituent services or legislative staff positions, and local government public engagement roles.

If you do apply, describe IEM work only where it truly involved writing, reviewing or publishing content, impartial fact-finding, or investigating stakeholder complaints, and use the posting's exact language.
Fit everything on two pages: give dates and hours per week for each job, and include full contact information for your references as the posting requests.
Submit well before the November 9, 2026 close, and answer every questionnaire item conservatively.
resume_bullets: Wrote and edited [type of publication/reports] on [emergency management topics] for [government client], ensuring accuracy and balance across [number] review cycles.
Investigated and resolved [number] stakeholder concerns about [program/process], evaluating opposing viewpoints and recommending corrective actions adopted by [client/leadership].
Briefed [audience, e.g., state/federal officials] on [policy issue], communicating complex findings clearly in writing and in [number] presentations.
interview_questions: Describe a time you investigated a complaint about fairness or accuracy and what you recommended.
How would you handle a DoD official pressuring editors to change or kill a story?
How do you stay impartial when evaluating opposing viewpoints from editors and readers?
How have digital and social media changed how audiences judge news credibility?
watch_outs: The core requirement of 10+ years in senior editorial leadership is very likely unmet based on what is on file.
International travel is required, and the summary says the job is in Washington, DC even though it is listed as remote, so confirm the duty arrangement.
Outside applicants rank behind NAF priority groups, and the position has no promotion potential and pays no incentives.
